page: Microsoft Azure D64pls_v5 is an ARM-based server instance belonging to the DPLSv5 family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is capable of mounting Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is relatively modest, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores falling into the lower tier. However, multi-core scaling is strong, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and high-throughput workloads like software compilation with Clang and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is strong at 4383.1 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read and write speeds remain average.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this instance as a compute-focused option where memory footprint is secondary. It exhibits strong performance in Redis SET operations, reaching 80.12 million operations per second, and maintains average throughput for static web serving and medium-model LLM inference. The lack of bundled local storage requires external disk attachment, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, and containerized microservices that benefit from high core density without requiring large memory allocations.
